Laboratory 3 - Visualization

3.1 Spatial Plots

Before we start, the library STRbook which provides example dataset should be installed.

install.packages("STRbook")

Then, two libraries should be loaded:

library(tidyverse)
library(STRbook)

We will use NOAA as the example. To load the NOAA datasets from the STRbook, we use the following code:

locs <- read.table(system.file("extdata", "Stationinfo.dat",
                               package = "STRbook"),
                   col.names = c("id", "lat", "lon"))
locs

locs contains the longitudes and latitudes of stations. Tmin_long contains records of minimum temperatures of each stations over the years.

data(Tmin_long, package = "STRbook")
Tmin_long

Next, we combine the station location with Tmin_long.

Tmin_long_loc = left_join(Tmin_long,locs, by="id")

We then create date variable with which R can order the data chronologically.

Tmin_long_loc$date <- as.Date(with(Tmin_long_loc,
                          paste(year, month, day, sep = "-")))

The dataset is quite large. We subset the dataset by focusing on data in year 1993 and in May to September.

Tmin_long_loc_sub <- filter(Tmin_long_loc, # subset the data
                 month %in% 5:9 & # May to September
                 year == 1993) # year of 1993

The first record has a Julian date of 728050, corresponding to 01 May 1993. To ease the following operations, we create a new variable t that is equal to 1 when julian == 728050 and increases by 1 for each day in the record. In addition, we focus on first day of each month.

Tmin_long_loc_sub$t <- Tmin_long_loc_sub$julian - 728049
Tmin_long_loc_sub <- subset(Tmin_long_loc_sub, day %in% c(1))
ggplot(Tmin_long_loc_sub) + # plot points
  geom_point(aes(x = lon,y = lat, # lon and lat
                 colour = z), # attribute color
             size = 2) + # make all points larger
  col_scale(name = "degF") + # attach color scale
  xlab("Longitude (deg)") + # x-axis label
  ylab("Latitude (deg)") + # y-axis label
  geom_path(data = map_data("state"), # add US states map
            aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group)) +
 facet_wrap(~date) + # facet by time
  coord_quickmap(xlim = c(-105, -75),
              ylim = c(25, 50))+ # zoom in
  theme_bw() # B&W theme

In addition to minimum temperature, you may explore the spatiotemporal pattern of dew point and precipitation data.
